body: **2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary** — changed §10 so that the epoch-boundary mutation audit (`run --mutants`) covers the CLI output-discipline invariants held in crate tests, replacing "the tests' mutation gate", after the founder removed the per-chunk and CI mutation gates. This is the origin of decision/mutation-audit-covers-crate-invariants and the reason the chunk runs no mutation itself: the Epoch 1 audit found the two `MAX_FRAME` survivors, and the next audit must catch them.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** (the client euid refusal's limit of proof) — added the Error recovery verification item saying a seam's wiring is read only by forced refusals in remove-the-guard runs that no committed test repeats, because a mutant replacing a seam's read survives every committed test. This is the precedent behind decision/client-euid-refusal-test-strategy and the one-off remove-the-guard control pattern this chunk uses on `read.rs:77` and `reply.rs:151` (`>` → `>=`).

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** — moved the CLI output-discipline evidence in CI into the `test` job's single instrumented `coverage` suite under `gate --require coverage,doctest`, with failures surfacing only as nextest failures in `suites[].failures[]`. This is the source of decision/a11y-cases-inside-coverage-suite, decision/gate-requires-coverage-doctest and decision/a11y-failures-are-nextest-failures. The chunk's new `viola-hyprland` tests land in that same gated suite.

**2026-10-16-remove-the-browser-leg** — removed the browser a11y leg. The cli and tui cases became nextest cases in the `coverage` suite. The failure condition is a `gate --require coverage,doctest` breach (`suite-failed`, `suite-skipped`, `suite-missing`, `artifact-missing`), `#[ignore]` is banned, and §11 bans any `suite` value or separate a11y driver outside `scripts/agent-run.* run`. This entry is the source of decision/a11y-gate-breach-fails-build, decision/zero-flakiness, decision/no-separate-a11y-driver and decision/a11y-runs-in-existing-test-suites. The new guard tests must not be `#[ignore]`d or skipped, and they need no a11y suite of their own.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** (the a11y cases' CI home, the one ubuntu-latest leg; the Linux-only platform line) — set the CI matrix to `[ubuntu-latest]`, with the `coverage` suite's `gate --require coverage,doctest` as the verdict and `scripts/agent-run.sh run` as the only runner. It also wrote the platform line: Linux only, with the 0.2.0 window features on Hyprland. This is the current form of decision/cli-invariants-pass-in-ci and decision/ci-test-gate-no-skips. The `viola-hyprland` tests run on that one leg.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** — added a §8 Timeout extensions entry for the `claude agents --json` read: a direct spawn with `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` and a 5 s kill, where a failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read fails open and the bound falls on viola's own child, never on the human. This is the precedent for the `MAX_FRAME + 1` drain and oversize pattern that `read_within` mirrors (`read.rs:121`), and for decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver / decision/time-bounds-never-on-human covering a bounded read of viola's own child.

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** — added `STATUSLINE_DEADLINE` to §8 as a bound on the user's own command, never on a keystroke, because the plan lists every bound viola holds and whom it falls on. This is one of the bounds named in decision/time-bounds-never-on-human. If the chunk changes the hyprctl read's time bound, the change has to be stated against that row.

**2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive** — recorded the first live reading of the takeover clause on Linux (a `wtype` key on a compositor the test started itself) as supplemental and never gating. This is the origin of decision/live-readings-never-gate. The chunk takes no live desktop step and uses only the fake `hyprctl`.

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** — added the takeover clause's second live reading (the founder's own key on the product binary), also supplemental and never gating. This confirms decision/live-readings-never-gate, so no gating case can rest on the real compositor or on a live `claude`.

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — this was the bounded-inputs chunk. On the a11y side it added only the outer-terminal half of the contained vt100 feed-panic case, leaving §4 P4 and the §3 keyboard harness unchanged. It is the precedent that a test-only bound pin like this chunk's moves no a11y clause unless it adds a human-facing byte.

**2026-11-08T20-32-52-wrap** (version census 0.2.0 — the frontend stubs retired) — made §5–§7 and the web keys N/A because viola has no web or graphical frontend, and gave the terminal fleet console's a11y scope to «Fleet a11y verification». This is the source of the picked absences and N/A lines: the Hyprland seam is a window feature with no rendered page, so it adds no a11y surface.

**2026-11-12T03-23-49-rows** — turned the master's text into rows (decision · contract · absence), each verified against the code. This is where every picked row's handle and wording comes from, including decision/no-assertions-for-internal-crates, which keeps `viola-hyprland` (an internal crate) without a11y assertions.

body: The viola-hyprland crate is an internal crate: its MAX_FRAME bounds are invariants held in crate tests, not user-facing output, so the new tests are crate tests rather than a11y assertions.
The mutation audit covers invariants held in crate tests: the chunk closes the audit's two missed mutants (> to >= on each MAX_FRAME bound), and each new test must be one that kills that mutant.
The new tests run inside the existing test suites under nextest; a failure of one is a nextest failure that fails the build, with no separate driver or suite value.
The CI test gate allows no skips: neither new test may be ignored, skipped or gated off in CI.
Zero flakiness, no retries: the exact-frame cases must be deterministic, the read's case driven only through the fake hyprctl with no live desktop, no real hyprctl and no live claude start.
Live readings never gate: nothing measured on a live compositor enters the tests; the bounded read's behaviour is replayed by the fake.
The gate requires coverage and doctest: the new tests run in the coverage suite the gate reads and must leave it green.
The oversize refusal and the Refused reply are asserted by their error variant (HyprlandError::Oversize, Refused), with no change to any error text or code word the seam carries.
The bounded read's time bound stays on the driver: the exact-frame case through the fake hyprctl must stay inside the read's existing deadline and add no wait that falls on a human.

Test-only chunk on the one Hyprland seam (viola-hyprland): pin the exact-frame case on both MAX_FRAME bounds the Epoch 1 code audit left as survivors (`>` mutated to `>=`).
The bounded read of a hyprctl reply: a test drives it through the fake hyprctl with a reply of exactly MAX_FRAME bytes (accepted, not oversize) and one of MAX_FRAME + 1 bytes (oversize).
The dispatch parse: a test gives parse_dispatch exactly MAX_FRAME bytes (not oversize; Refused, as they are not the success text) and MAX_FRAME + 1 bytes (oversize).

body: The bounded read of a hyprctl reply (read_within): a reply of exactly MAX_FRAME bytes is accepted, one of MAX_FRAME + 1 bytes is refused as oversize, the child's stdout drained only up to MAX_FRAME + 1 bytes.
The dispatch reply parse (parse_dispatch): exactly MAX_FRAME bytes are not oversize and read as Refused (not the success text); MAX_FRAME + 1 bytes are oversize.

The frame cap every bounded external reader keeps: a reader of an external process's output or reply stops at MAX_FRAME and refuses more, and the new tests pin that boundary byte for byte on both sites.

The remove-the-guard witness each new guard test owes: a one-off bounded control that mutates the guard site itself (`>` to `>=`), names the test's case by its name alone, reaches that case past fail-fast under a kill deadline, and holds only when that case ran and failed.

The mutation audit at the epoch boundary whose two survivors this chunk closes: the next audit's mutation of either bound must be caught by a test, while no mutation run, local or dispatched, happens inside the chunk.
The read's test reaches hyprctl only through the fake hyprctl, a real stub executable at the seam the read's tests already use; no real hyprctl, no live desktop step and no live claude start.
Doubles only at the product's own seams: the Hyprland seam is the one seam the fake replaces, and the dispatch parse, a pure function, is called directly with its bytes.

The bound values the tests use come from the product constant MAX_FRAME (exactly it and one more), not from a copied number, and the expected outcomes (accepted, Refused, oversize) are written as literal oracles.
The read's test waits on the fake child under a bounded deadline, with no sleep synchronisation and no retry.
The clients reply parse's bound stays pinned by its existing exact-frame test (takes MAX_FRAME bytes, refuses one more as oversize); the chunk reads it and does not re-pin it.
Test-only change: no product line moves unless a new test proves one wrong, in which case the fix folds into the chunk with its own acceptance; no requirement added and no capability claimed.

body_fields.convention: every new test function is named by the test-function naming rule (the behaviour and its outcome in the name)
every new unit test lives inline in its source file's test module
every new test synchronises without sleeps and is never retried on failure
every new test writes its oracles as literals and holds no shared mutable state, running in parallel with the rest

The fake agent standing in for the claude CLI, its command line, receipts, turn scripts and recorded hook fixtures: the chunk's only double is the fake hyprctl.
Hook, dialog, send, wheel, budget, statusline, list, revive and run-start contracts and their exit codes: no product surface beyond the Hyprland seam's two bounds is reached.
The test harness commands and their documents (boot, cleanup, status, session record, supervisor, pre-push, run --mutants verdicts): no mutation run happens and the chunk adds no harness surface.
The declined mutation units of viola-e2e and viola: they stay out, waiting on a pipeline mend.
Performance budgets and hyperfine timing of hooks: the chunk times nothing.
Process log lines and their fields, the event log and diagnostics schemas: the chunk adds no log line and no event.
CI artifacts, their retention and the artifact secret scan: the chunk adds no CI job and no artifact.
Fixture recording, scrubbing and hygiene of recorded claude payloads: the chunk records no fixture.
